summary: Aberdeen International Airport is located in Dyce, approximately 7 miles northwest of Aberdeen city centre, serving as the principal gateway to northeast Scotland. It is renowned as the main helicopter and fixed-wing hub for the North Sea oil and gas industry, earning Aberdeen its reputation as the energy capital of Europe. The airport features a single modern terminal handling around 3 million passengers annually.
faqs:
Q: How far is Aberdeen Airport from the city centre?
A: The airport is located about 7 miles (11 km) northwest of Aberdeen city centre in Dyce, typically a 20-30 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Does Aberdeen Airport have rail connections?
A: Yes, Dyce railway station is located near the airport and offers regular ScotRail services to Aberdeen city centre and onward connections to Inverness and the rest of Scotland.

Q: What airlines operate from Aberdeen Airport?
A: Major carriers include British Airways, easyJet, Loganair, KLM, Ryanair, and Wizz Air, offering domestic, European, and some long-haul routes.

Q: Is there a direct bus service to the airport?
A: Yes, Stagecoach and other operators run regular bus services connecting the airport to Aberdeen city centre and surrounding areas.
transport_tips: The 727 Stagecoach bus provides a direct and affordable link between the airport and Aberdeen city centre, running frequently throughout the day. Taxis and ride-share services are readily available outside the terminal, typically costing £15-20 to the city centre. For those driving, the airport is just off the A96 and offers short-term and long-term parking options with online pre-booking discounts.
local_tip: If you have a layover or arrive early, the airport's Executive Lounge offers stunning views of the airfield and is an ideal spot for helicopter-spotting, as Aberdeen handles more helicopter movements than almost any other UK airport due to its oil and gas connections.
